parts:
Hello all,

I was wondering if there was any update on the issue regarding f (any(dCOV < 0)) reported on the thread below?

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/lavaan/if$20(any(dCOV$20%3C$200))/lavaan/J-4InyEo8i8/HoeWtcqWAQAJ

I keep running into it when using  std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "theta" parameterization with LSAT data. For other parameterizations, listed below, I observe no issue.

 std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "delta"
 std.lv=TRUE& parameterization = "delta"
 std.lv=TRUE & parameterization = "theta"

A sample code is attached. Is there something missing in my model for the std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "theta" parameterization?

Looking forward to hearing from you,

Hugo

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in if (any(dCOV < 0)) - Transversal example - std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "theta"
parts:
I was wondering if there was any update on the issue regarding f (any(dCOV < 0)) reported on the thread below?

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/lavaan/if$20(any(dCOV$20%3C$200))/lavaan/J-4InyEo8i8/HoeWtcqWAQAJ
You can post on the same thread to try to get a response from the original poster, but they never responded to my query about whether it was resolved.
Is there something missing in my model for the std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "theta" parameterization?

I think there is not nearly enough missing from your syntax.  I recall mentioning before that you are unnecessarily defining constraints that are redundant with the selected parameterizations.  For example, this constraint:

mean1+lmbd1*lv1mean==0

is unnecessarily complex.  Because lmbd1 == 1 and mean1 == 0, the only solution is lv1mean == 0.  Likewise, it then follows that the remaining constraints on intercepts are redundant because the lambdas are always multiplied by zero. So mean2 + lmbd2*lv1mean == 0 simplifies to mean2 == 0 (and the same for other indicators).  So you have gone the long way around to fixing all means to zero, which is what the software does anyway.  Perhaps there is another condition where you plan to fix lv1mean to a different arbitrary value?  There may be nothing "wrong" with your model specification, but it is simultaneously redundant and could place quite complex constraints on the optimizer when searching the parameter space for values that just end up being 0 or 1 anyway.

The only place in the lavaan source code that "dCOV" appears is in the hidden objective function, which iteratively searches for optimal parameters.  dCOV is the diagonal of the model-implied covariance matrix at a particular iteration.  At the point it returned an error, the optimizer appears to have gone way off the rails, searching the parameter space where psi[1,1] is quite negative, with model-implied latent scales of NA for all but x1.  This leads the model-implied Sigma to have missing values on the diagonal, hence the error.  I dump()ed the estimates (in GLIST) and attached the R syntax so you can see where the optimizer was looking when it failed.  Notice that $alpha is also negative, despite the fact that your constraints imply it is simply zero.  If you take out all the mean-structure constraints from your syntax, your model runs fine (with all intercepts == 0 by default, as implied in your script).  Thus, your method of defining complex redundant constraints appears to simply put too much pressure on the optimizer in this case.  You can see how complex the constraint function is in the object lavm...@ceq.function, and compare that to the less complex function when the model runs without specifying mean-structure parameters/constraints (mod2ind4lv1.fit@Mod...@ceq.function).  Removing the redundant constraints on residual variances would make it even simpler, making the optimizer's job easier, although those constraints are as problematic because they only involve 1 parameter (in the theta parameterization, at least).  In contrast, there are infinite possible solutions to your model-implied indicator-mean constraints (despite the implication that they simply be zero, you are forcing the optimizer to discover that iteratively, which will not always work -- better starting values might help). 

You can find technical details about optimization with equality constraints here: https://lavaan.ugent.be/notes/lavaan_eq_constraints.pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Makes a lot of sense.  I was trying to understand lavaan behavior when estimating y* in the transversal mode so that I understand what it does in longitudinal mode. It is like this, right?

std.lv=TRUE& parameterization = "delta" ->   y*~ N(0,1)
std.lv=TRUE & parameterization = "theta" ->  y*~ N(0,psi*lambda^2+1)
std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "delta" -> y*~ N(0,1)
std.lv=FALSE & parameterization = "theta"->  y*~ N(0,psi*lambda^2+1)

Kind regards,

Hugo
